title: runtime/scheduler: add baseline explainability metrics (queue wait histograms, batch composition, backpressure events)
author: Julian Moore
description:
Motivation: Baseline suite runs are currently hard to explain when p95/p99 moves (especially under bursty concurrency / mixed prompt lengths). We can see end-to-end latency regressions, but not whether the tail came from queueing, batch composition shifts, prefill/decode imbalance, or explicit backpressure/load-shedding. This PR adds the minimal scheduler metrics needed by the Q1'26 perf baseline effort to make tail behavior explainable and to support variance triage.

What’s included (server-side, scheduler layer): (1) Queue wait histograms: request queue wait time split by phase and by outcome. New metrics: redwood_runtime_sched_queue_wait_ms_bucket{phase="prefill|decode", outcome="scheduled|dropped"}, plus _sum/_count. Queue wait is measured from enqueue -> admitted into a GPU batch (prefill) and from decode-ready -> admitted (decode). (2) Batch composition counters/gauges: batch sizes and token composition to correlate tail shifts with changed batching. New metrics: redwood_runtime_sched_batch_size{phase="prefill|decode"} (histogram), redwood_runtime_sched_batch_prompt_tokens (histogram), redwood_runtime_sched_batch_decode_tokens (histogram), redwood_runtime_sched_active_sequences (gauge), redwood_runtime_sched_kv_cache_pages_in_batch (histogram). (3) Backpressure + load-shedding events: explicit counters to distinguish “slow” vs “throttled” and to pinpoint reasons. New metric: redwood_runtime_sched_backpressure_events_total{reason="queue_depth|gpu_oom_guard|max_inflight|deadline_miss|tenant_fairness"}. Reasons are a fixed enum to avoid cardinality blowups.

Cardinality/overhead: No per-tenant labels, no route labels, no model labels at this layer (those already exist upstream). All new labels are bounded enums (phase/outcome/reason). Histograms use the runtime standard latency bucket set (per Observability standards) with an additional short-range set for queue wait (0-5s). Overhead measured in local perf smoke: +0.3-0.6% CPU in scheduler thread under 2k rps synthetic; memory impact negligible.

How this will be used: Perf baseline harness (benchmark-lab) will scrape/collect these metrics alongside TTFT/TPOT. For a p99 regression, we can now answer: did queue wait shift (scheduler/pressure) vs did batch composition shift (batching heuristics) vs did backpressure fire (explicit throttle) vs is it kernel/runtime execution.

Testing: Added unit tests for label enums + backpressure reason mapping; integration test asserts metric presence on a small scheduler simulation; manual validation in staging by forcing queue buildup and verifying histogram movement. Docs: added metric definitions to runtime/metrics catalog and linked from the baseline instrumentation checklist.

Rollout: Guarded behind feature flag runtime.telemetry.scheduler_baseline_metrics (default on for perf-canary + benchmark environments, off for prod until SRE sign-off).
